[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:04] Mark: yeah loud and clear, thanks Jordan
[00:07] Jordan: cool, quick intros, i'm Jordan AE, Priya is our SE who'll own the harness integration, Aisha is here for adapter questions. Mark, Evelyn, Liam?
[00:18] Mark: Mark Duarte, CTO, i'll be the exec sponsor but Evelyn leads the infra work.
[00:22] Evelyn: hi all, Evelyn, platform lead, we'll own the tests and the SRE handoff.
[00:28] Liam: Liam O'Neal, SRE, i'll be running the traces and helping with env access.
[00:33] Jordan: great. Goal for today is to agree success criteria and the practical steps for hooking up your existing scripts to our harness and decide streaming vs non-streaming baseline.
[00:45] Priya: i'll go over the harness adapter expectations, but first can you confirm the customer script shape? i saw in the doc some mixed sync calls with a streaming client, is that accurate?
[00:56] Sara: yes we've got two runners, one that simulates long-form chat (streaming) and one that's batch single-shot prompts, both from the same script repo.
[01:06] Priya: ok that's helpful — for streaming runs we need client-level chunking and to respect keepalive so we don't artificially inflate concurrent sessions. also we recommend a warmup that exercises the KV cache to avoid cold-start tail latency skew.
[01:21] Mark: quick question on KV cache warmup: is that an explicit prefill step? or do you want us to replay past traffic?
[01:29] Priya: either works, but prefer a short replay of 5-10% of typical traffic across the top N users so we pre-populate embeddings and the KV layers. note sometimes transcription shows "K V cache" or other typos in our docs, it's the same thing.
[01:44] Aisha: we'll share a small helper script that can transform your trace into warmup calls, link will be in the README.
[01:50] Jordan: action item — Jordan will share harness README and sample adapter after the call. link: https://redwood.example/harness-readme (placeholder)
[02:00] Evelyn: curious about throughput sizing — you have guidance for Dedicated pool sizing vs hosted? our target is 250 req/s peak with 95th latency < 350ms for batch and streaming tail < 600ms.
[02:14] Priya: important nuance: streaming tail latency is sensitive to chunk size and model seq length. for mixed workloads, we recommend partitioning routes by sla bucket. for 250 rps can you share token-per-request distribution?
[02:28] Mark: average tokens 120, p95 tokens 800 — that's because we have long discharge summaries for some calls.
[02:35] Priya: with 120 avg and those p95s, our baseline for quantized open models should be X GPU per 1200 concurrent tokens — we'll put numbers in the sizing doc. but rough math says Dedicated pool of 8 A100-equivalents for stable 250rps with some burst headroom, subject to final harness numbers.
[02:55] Liam: can we run an on-prem throughput run? security says we need to validate within our VPC footprint before committing.
[03:02] Jordan: yes we can do a private pilot or bring your scripts to our dedicated staging in your VPC. two paths: 1) run in your infra using our on-prem package, 2) run in Redwood private staging with network peering. both have pros/cons re: setup time.
[03:18] Sara: what's typical time to get the harness adapter integrated? our devs are small, 1-2 people.
[03:24] Priya: usually 2-4 days to adapt scripts and validate flows, then a 1-2 day baseline run and a 1 day streaming stress test. so total ~1 week for initial POC runs if we have traces ready.
[03:36] Jordan: timeline check — we'd aim to have sample trace and scripts by Friday (Nov 5), adapter work next week, baseline runs week of Nov 8. does that align?
[03:45] Mark: yes Nov 5 to share artifacts is ok. security will need SOC2 artifacts before we schedule the staging run.
[03:51] Jordan: i'll send SOC2 matrix and security checklist as part of next steps.
[03:56] Evelyn: on acceptance criteria, we'd like throughput gates, error budgets < 0.1% 5xx, and output quality checks for hallucination rates below 2% on a fixed eval set.
[04:07] Priya: we'll map those to tests: throughput pass/fail, latency SLOs per route, and an eval harness to run the quality prompts. can you share eval sets?
[04:15] Sara: yes we'll share a 500 prompt eval and the scoring rubric by Nov 6.
[04:21] Liam: slightly worried about streaming fallthrough: if streaming fails mid-session, does Redwood support automatic fallthrough to non-streaming?
[04:29] Aisha: yes we have fallthrough policies — we can configure client-side half-close handling or server-side fallbacks. Priya will document recommended policy.
[04:40] Jordan: competitor question — anyone considering Anthropic or Bedrock?
[04:43] Mark: we're evaluating multiple vendors, Bedrock for integrated infra and Anthropic for safety features, but this POC is about performance and cost.
[04:52] Priya: noted. we'll record cost-per-token estimates for the harness runs and show Dedicated vs hosted delta.
[04:58] Mark: what about cold-start tail latency? our SLA needs 95th < 350ms, but p99 can spike.
[05:06] Priya: cold starts happen when KV isn't populated or model weights spin up; for production you can use pre-warmed pools and prefix caching. as part of the harness we'll run cold-start tests to capture p99 tail and then the warmup-enabled runs to show improvement.
[05:20] Jordan: ok let's recap next steps and owners. Jordan will send README + SOC2 artifacts, Priya will review scripts and produce stream vs non-stream runbook, Liam will share traces and evals. We aim to run baseline week of Nov 8.
[05:36] Mark: sounds good, thanks all.
[05:38] Jordan: thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the run window and a short checklist.
[05:44] (meeting ends)
